name: Eastern Michigan Industries
old_description: Eastern Michigan Industries was started in 2000.  We started with the desire to produce hugh quality fabrications for the tooling industry.  Our mission is quality to always be considdered over timing.  It is our desire to fulfill your companys needs with the best combination between Cost, Timing and Quality!!  We are however human and if mistakes are made rest assured that we will do what ever it takes to fix the problem and make it right!
about:
Eastern Michigan Industries was founded in 2000 in Warren, Michigan, with the goal of producing high-quality fabrications for the tooling industry. The company operates from two facilities totaling more than 45,000 square feet and employs approximately 25 people.

The shop provides full-service fabrication including plate burning up to 12 inches thick, high-definition plasma cutting up to 108 by 520 inches, Blanchard grinding up to 156 inches, and machining envelopes as large as 144 by 672 inches. It handles structural steel, plate, stainless steel, and aluminum weldments, with weight capacity up to 50,000 pounds. In-house inspection includes an AWS Certified Welding Inspector qualified to D1.1, D1.2, D14.1, API 1104, and aircraft codes, plus ASNT Level II personnel for liquid penetrant and magnetic particle testing.

Customers span military, automotive, aerospace, marine, residential, wastewater treatment, and general tooling sectors. Typical projects include robot risers, machine bases, frames, burnout shapes, stairways, platforms, balconies, and railings.

name: Eastman Screen Printing
old_description: Founded in 2022, Eastman Screen Printing was a dream long in the making…
about:
Eastman Screen Printing was founded in 2022 in Concord, New Hampshire, as a locally owned shop. The venture began as a long-held dream of managers Ron Dulong and Sam Mostue, who envisioned a neighborhood screen-printing service where customers could watch their promotional products being crafted by hand, much like a local candy shop.

The company provides screen printing on apparel and tote bags using plastisol, water-based, and discharge inks; embroidery with digitizing, 3D foam, and puff styles; signs, banners, and vehicle graphics printed on vinyl; and business printing including cards, brochures, flyers, and direct-mail services such as EDDM. All production is done in-house, with order volumes ranging from a single piece to over 10,000 units and rush turnaround available.

Eastman serves businesses and organizations throughout Concord and central New Hampshire. Clients include local companies such as Out on a Limb Tree Care LLC, school theatre programs, and corporate customers needing uniforms, event gear, and promotional items. The shop also handles retail-style orders for individuals and small groups.

The founders emphasize transparent, in-house production that lets clients see the work in progress, full-service support from design through delivery, and personalized service with upfront pricing. Their stated goal is to make Concord a more creative community by offering a friendly, capable local alternative for custom printing and branding.

name: Eaton Sales & Service LLC
old_description: Excellent service and a wide surplus of inventory. Attention to every detail. It’s no wonder they’ve been in business since 1919.
about:
Founded in 1919 in Casper, Wyoming, Eaton Sales & Service traces its origins to the Eaton Metal Products Company, which was active in petroleum equipment as early as the 1950s. The business re‑entered the petroleum market in the 1980s through a series of acquisitions and internal growth, expanding into a full‑service sales, installation, and service operation across the Rocky Mountain region.

The company manufactures both above‑ground and underground fuel storage tanks and provides a complete range of petroleum equipment services, including sales, installation, construction, fueling‑system maintenance, lubrication, mechanical‑integrity inspection, and distribution. It operates from nine locations spanning Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico, and Arizona, and reports more than 500,000 completed projects and 30,000 active customers.

Eaton serves retail and commercial fueling stations, agricultural operations, marinas, and aviation facilities. Its customer base includes major oil companies, big‑box retailers, grocery‑store chains, and independent fueling operators throughout the Rocky Mountain region.

The firm emphasizes 24/7 emergency response, a team of factory‑ and regulatory‑certified technicians trained on equipment from suppliers such as Wayne, Veeder‑Root, OPW, and Franklin, and an engineering group that supports custom tank design. Its stated mission is to exceed customer expectations with responsive, cost‑effective manufacturing and service solutions.

name: Eckhart Woodworking
old_description: Welcome to Eckhart, where tradition meets innovation in the world of custom woodworking. As a family-owned business, we take pride in our heritage of exquisite craftsmanship and Amish construction expertise. Specializing in custom molding, restorations, interior and exterior doors, gun cabinets, restaurant and bar interiors, custom live edge conference room tables, merchant display units as well as cutting-edge CNC work, we bring a touch of timeless artistry to every project.
about:
Eckhart Woodworking is a family-owned custom woodworking shop based in Monroe, Indiana, founded in 1989. The company began as a family operation rooted in Amish construction expertise, blending traditional craftsmanship with modern technology.

The shop specializes in custom molding (offering over 1,200 profiles), interior and exterior doors, gun cabinets, restaurant and bar interiors, live-edge conference tables, merchant display units, and modern design furniture. Its capabilities include custom milling, CNC machining, and hand-finished furniture assembly, serving both one-off commissions and larger commercial projects.

Customers range from homeowners seeking restoration trim matches and custom entry doors to hospitality contractors outfitting restaurants and bars, retailers needing display fixtures, and corporate clients ordering conference tables. The company also serves firearm enthusiasts with custom gun cabinets and handles historical restoration work.

Eckhart emphasizes heritage craftsmanship, close collaboration on custom designs, premium wood sourcing, and on-time delivery. Its stated mission focuses on providing second-chance employment opportunities, aiming to create positive community impact through its hiring practices.

name: Eco Woodworks
old_description: Eco Woodworks is an Olympia based woodworking shop that specializes in custom carpentry & historical restoration. For over two decades, our goal has been to work with customers to transform their homes into more beautiful & usable spaces. We exercise sustainability & focus on preservation wherever possible throughout our entire process. We believe in a culture of community & educational outreach through local partnerships.
about:
Eco Woodworks operates from Tumwater, Washington, serving the greater Olympia area. The shop was established more than two decades ago as a custom carpentry and historical restoration business, though the exact founding year and founders’ names are not publicly documented. The company has remained independently owned, focusing on woodworking for residential and historic properties.

The shop provides a range of woodworking services, including custom carpentry, historical restoration, wood window restoration and repair, new wood window manufacturing, custom cabinet and furniture making, door fabrication, finish carpentry remodeling, and handcrafted mantels and millwork. All pieces are built in the company’s own shop, with projects spanning fully custom to semi‑custom designs. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are disclosed.

Eco Woodworks serves homeowners, historic property stewards, and contractors seeking period‑appropriate woodwork. The company has worked on historic sites around Olympia following the Secretary of the Interior’s Federal Guidelines for preservation, and it regularly restores windows, doors, and millwork for historic homes. Its cabinet and furniture projects address both functional and aesthetic needs in residential remodels.

The firm emphasizes sustainability and preservation throughout its process, aiming to reduce energy consumption through weatherized window solutions without compromising original views. It also cites a culture of community and educational outreach through local partnerships as a core differentiator, and it balances budget and desire by offering both fully custom and semi‑custom build options.

name: EcoGen America
old_description: Founded in 2016, we have expanded from regional roots to a nationwide data-driven platform, accumulating nearly a decade of direct solar industry exposure.
about:
EcoGen America is headquartered in Camden, Delaware, and was founded in 2016 by Trevor Guilday. The company began as a regional effort to connect homeowners with local solar installers and expanded nationwide by 2022 to cover all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico. In 2025 the platform was completely rebuilt with a homeowner-first brand, strict verification frameworks, and updated data infrastructure. Leadership includes CEO Dean Mahmoud, who has worked in residential solar since 2021, and a core team overseeing data analytics, partnerships, technology, and content.

The company operates an independent solar education and research platform. It publishes the EcoGen Solar Cost Index, a state-level price benchmark built on Department of Energy laboratory benchmarks, Bureau of Labor Statistics wage data, Energy Information Administration electricity-use figures, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory transacted-price data. The index is calibrated against current marketplace quotes and proprietary cost modeling. EcoGen also maintains a verified installer network; partners must hold an active state license, demonstrate installation activity in the state, and offer a workmanship warranty covering roof penetrations. The company processes quote requests from homeowners and earns referral fees from partner installers, while keeping editorial content independent of advertising relationships.

EcoGen serves residential homeowners exploring solar adoption across the United States. Its guides address system pricing, federal and state incentives, financing options, and installer selection. The platform’s matching service connects homeowners with solar providers in their area; as of September 2026 the network included six commercial partners. The company’s data and methodology are referenced by contributing experts in solar policy, tax credits, and clean energy journalism.

EcoGen was created to close a transparency gap in the solar industry, where homeowners faced high-pressure sales tactics without reliable, unbiased data. The founder’s stated goal is to provide free educational resources, up-to-date pricing insights, and personalized quote comparisons so that homeowners know exactly what they are buying before signing a contract. The company emphasizes public data sources, a published verification methodology, and a revenue model that does not influence editorial recommendations.

name: Ecotex – Healthcare Laundry Services, New Mexico
old_description: Ecotex is a privately owned, family-led company that has been delivering laundry services people count on since 1959. Built over three generations of the Bartsch family, we are a multi-generational family enterprise focused on creating and maintaining productive long-term partnerships with large healthcare customers.
about:
Ecotex Healthcare Linen Service, headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, traces its roots to 1959 when Eldon and Ruth Bartsch opened Southgate Cleaners, a small local cleaning service. The company remains privately owned and family-led, now under the third generation of the Bartsch family, with Bryan Bartsch serving as president and CEO.

The company operates multiple regional laundry facilities, including what it describes as the largest healthcare laundry plant in North America. With a workforce of more than 1,700 employees, Ecotex processes over one million pieces of hygienically clean healthcare linen daily. Its services span healthcare laundering, surgical sterilization, linen management, and on-site linen distribution, supported by highly automated tunnel washing systems and environmentally friendly practices such as water conservation and eco-friendly detergents.

Ecotex serves hospitals, long-term care facilities, and medical centers across Canada and North America. Its customer base includes large healthcare systems that rely on the company for patient apparel, bedding, surgical linens, PPE, scrubs, and infection-control textiles.

The company emphasizes its family ownership as a differentiator, stating it enables quick decision-making, long-term reinvestment, and direct issue resolution without layers of approval. Ecotex also highlights its Hygienically Clean and Clean Green certifications, along with HLAC accreditation, as markers of its commitment to quality and sustainability.

name: Edesia Nutrition
old_description: We produce an entire range of therapeutic foods to treat and prevent malnutrition. Since 2010, Edesia has shipped to 65 countries with global partners.
about:
Edesia Nutrition was founded in 2010 in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, by Navyn Salem, who serves as CEO. The organization was named after the Roman goddess of food and began after Salem was inspired by a 60 Minutes segment on Plumpy'Nut's impact in Niger. It operates as a nonprofit manufacturer of therapeutic foods.

The company produces a full range of ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTF) to treat and prevent malnutrition. Its Rhode Island factory manufactures up to 88 million pounds of product annually, using ingredients sourced from 17 U.S. states. The facility handles formulation, production, and packaging of lifesaving foods such as Plumpy'Nut.

Edesia serves humanitarian organizations, governments, and global health partners, delivering to communities in crisis across more than 65 countries. Its customers include UN agencies, NGOs, and donor governments that distribute the foods in emergency and development settings. The company also coordinates last-mile logistics by land, air, and sea.

Edesia was built on the belief that no child should suffer from malnutrition when solutions exist. It differentiates itself through an integrated model that combines domestic manufacturing, a $9 million innovation fund supporting research in 13 countries, policy advocacy, and country-specific coalition building to scale nutrition programs.
